title: Patient Payment Plan Returned-Payment Fee Amount
content:
The returned-payment fee of a Patient Payment Plan is the tier's returned-payment fee where the plan's automatic payments are drawn from a bank account, and nothing for a card draft where the tier does not apply the returned-payment fee to declined cards; it is rounded to the cent.

## How the figure is set

| Element | Basis |
|---|---|
| Draft charged | The installment whose automatic draft most recently came back unpaid; the fee carries that installment's due date |
| Source of the automatic payments | The automatic payment method on the plan: a bank account (ACH) or a card |
| Amount where drawn from a bank account | The tier's returned-payment fee, from the Patient Payment Plan fee schedule |
| Amount for a card draft | Nothing where the tier does not apply the returned-payment fee to declined cards (fee schedule) |
| Rounding | To the nearest cent once, on the final amount |

## Worked figures (hypothetical tier with a returned-payment fee of 25.00 that does not apply the fee to declined cards)

- Automatic payments drawn by ACH from a checking account; the draft for the installment due 2026-04-15 came back unpaid. Fee: 25.00, carrying the due date 2026-04-15.
- Automatic payments drawn from a card; the card draft failed. Fee: nothing.
- A hypothetical tier whose returned-payment fee is 0.00: an ACH draft that came back gives a fee of 0.00.
